cards.text: Friend, this is John, telling us what he saw (Revelation 1:1, 9). Last time, the dragon, that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, was hurled to the earth and ended up standing on the shore of the sea (Revelation 12:9, 17). Now John says, "Then I saw a beast with ten horns and seven heads rising out of the sea."

cards.question: The beast John sees rising out of the sea has ten royal crowns, and they sit on its ten horns.

cards.text: On its seven heads are blasphemous names, and the beast is like a leopard, with the feet of a bear and the mouth of a lion. Friend, I use a MUSTACHE for hands, and even I'm looking at this thing going, WHAT?

cards.question: Who gives the beast from the sea power, a throne and great authority?

cards.text: Then John notices one of the beast's heads. It appeared to have been mortally wounded.

cards.question: The mortal wound on the beast's head is ___.
When the beast's mortal wound is healed, the whole world marvels and follows the beast.

cards.text: And the people don't stop at following. They worship the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?"

cards.question: The people worship the beast from the sea, but they never worship the dragon.
The crowd asks, "Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?" What are they saying about the beast?

answers.text: It will lose a war soon

cards.text: The beast was given a mouth to speak arrogant and blasphemous words. Friend, catch that little phrase: "was given."

cards.question: The beast is also given authority to act for ___ months.
When the beast opens its mouth, it speaks blasphemies against ___ and slanders His name.

cards.text: Then it gets heavy. The beast was permitted to wage war against the saints and to conquer them.

cards.question: How far does the authority given to the beast from the sea reach?

answers.text: Every tribe and people and tongue and nation
Only the cities along the shore of the sea
Only the people who already follow the dragon

cards.text: John says all who dwell on the earth will worship the beast: all whose names have not been written, from the foundation of the world, in a book belonging to the Lamb who was slain. The Lamb is Jesus (John 1:29).

cards.question: What is the book called that belongs to the Lamb who was slain?

cards.text: Then John calls out, "He who has an ear, let him hear:" Whoever is destined for captivity will go into captivity, and whoever is to die by the sword will be killed by the sword.

cards.question: After that hard word about captivity and the sword, what does John say this is a call for?

answers.text: The perseverance and faith of the saints
The saints to strike back at the beast
The saints to flee into the wilderness

cards.text: Then John says, "Then I saw another beast rising out of the earth." This one has two horns like a lamb, and I bet you're thinking, okay, this one looks gentle.

cards.question: The beast from the earth has two horns like a lamb. But it speaks like what?

cards.text: This second beast exercised all the authority of the first beast, the one whose mortal wound had been healed.

cards.question: The second beast gets the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast.

cards.text: The second beast performs great signs, even causing fire from heaven to come down to earth in the presence of the people. FIRE from HEAVEN, and I need a preheat and a timer just to warm up one oven.

cards.question: Because of the signs it was given to perform, the second beast ___ those who dwell on the earth.

cards.text: Then it tells the people to make something for the first beast, the one that had been wounded by the sword and yet had lived.

cards.question: What does the second beast tell the people to make for the first beast?

cards.text: Then the second beast was permitted to give breath to the image of the first beast, so the image could speak.

cards.question: The speaking image could cause all who refused to worship it to be ___.

cards.text: Then the second beast requires all people, small and great, rich and poor, free and slave, to receive a mark.

cards.question: Where does the second beast require people to receive the mark?
The mark from the second beast matters, because without it no one could ___ or ___.

cards.text: No mark, no buying, no selling. Picture your card getting declined at every single register in town.

cards.question: The mark people must have to buy or sell is the name of the beast or the number of its name.

cards.text: Then John says, "Here is a call for wisdom:" the one who has insight should calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man. Friend, I lose count of the chocolate chips stuck in my own mustache, so I'm listening close.

cards.question: What does John say the number of the beast is?

findings.problem: The opening card says who is speaking (John) and what is going on, but not who John is speaking to. Revelation is addressed to the seven churches (Revelation 1:4, 11).

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The question writes 'slanders His name' with a capital H. That capital points straight to God and rules out 'the dragon' and 'the sea' before the baker reasons anything out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Revelation 13:6 also says the beast slanders God's tabernacle, those who dwell in heaven. No card tells this, so the baker never hears it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has only one joke (card 3) across its eight story cards. Cards 5, 8, 14, 16 and 18 read as plain narration with almost no Papa Dorin voice. Some of these moments are heavy, such as the saints being conquered, but a few others could carry a real laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'pardoned' isn't believable. An image that causes everyone who refuses to worship it to be pardoned makes no sense, so the card is really a choice between two answers.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The card opens by repeating card 13's answer ('No mark, no buying, no selling') and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The 'name or number' detail is left for card 15 to ask, so this card is a recap.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
